facebook.content_angle: Pull buoy dependency — how relying on a pull buoy masks a broken body position and quietly destroys your freestyle splits the moment it is removed
facebook.post_text:
Remove the pull buoy. Watch your hips sink. 🎯

Most club swimmers swim their best laps with a pull buoy — then wonder why their freestyle falls apart in a race. The buoy is not making you faster. It is hiding the problem.

👉 A pull buoy artificially lifts your hips, masking a weak core position and a kick that is not doing its job
👉 Swimmers who rely on it regularly lose up to 3 seconds per 50m the moment it is removed in competition
👉 Real race-ready body position has to be earned through hip-driven kick mechanics — not borrowed from foam

Your gear should perform because your body is ready for it. 💪

✔️ Audit your next session — swim a 200m with and without the pull buoy and time the difference honestly
✔️ If your hips drop without it, prioritise six-beat kick drills and core tension work before your next race block
✔️ Build the body position first — then let a race suit do what it is actually designed to do

How much time are you losing between pull buoy sessions and race day?
